To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mouse model with complete deletion of exon 3 of the ERβ gene (ERβST−/L−), which is devoid of all ERβ transcripts, exhibits a reproductive phenotype similar to that of other ERβ mutants, but does not exhibit any other phenotype.
a mouse ERβ mutant, in which exon 2 and exon 3 have been cleanly deleted, is completely normal, with the exception of male and females sterility.
a mouse mutant in which exon 4 of the ERβ gene is deleted is sterile, but otherwise normal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ERβ in the mouse.
understanding the role of the estrogen receptor β (ERβ) in reproduction and in nonreproductive tissues and organs.
the role of estrogen receptors in the development and homeostenesis of the major body organs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERβ is not necessary for the normal development and homeostatic functions of all organs in the mouse, with the notable exceptions of reproduction and bone.
ERβ is dispensable in mice.
, in mice, ERβ is required only for male and female reproduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERβ is a reproductive hormone receptor, but is not an essential regulator of non-reproductive organ homeostasis.
the phenotypic effects of ERβ inactivation are restricted to the gonads, and are more pronounced in males than in females.
ERβ plays a role in female and male reproduction, and in the ovary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of ERβ, the remaining ERα is sufficient to maintain the homeostasis of all organs.
the ERβ knockout mouse phenotype is not a reliable model to study the function of ERβ in the mouse.

the phenotypes reported by various groups for different ERβ mutants are not necessarily due to the absence of ERβ but may be the result of the alternative splicing of transcripts that occur in the ERβ mutants.
